subject: spanish
title: Stamp 3: Intertextualidad and Voice
welcome_lead: Stamp intertextuality and the layered voices of literary texts.
meta_desc: A-Level Spanish adventure on intertextualidad, voz narrativa, and stylistic registers.

concepts.def: Intertextuality; relationships between texts through allusion, quotation, or pastiche.
Narrative voice; the manner and tone in which the narrator communicates.
Register; level of formality (culto, coloquial, vulgar).
Pastiche; imitation of another author's style, sometimes affectionate.
Parody; comic or critical imitation that exaggerates conventions.
Hypertext; in Genette's terms, a text derived from a previous hypotext.

walkthroughs.body_html: Julia Kristeva coined the term in 1966. Every text is in dialogue with others. Cervantes's Don Quijote parodies chivalric romances, embedding fragments of them in its own narrative.
In La colmena (Cela, 1951), characters speak in distinct registers reflecting class and context. Identifying register helps interpret character relationships and authorial stance.
Pastiche imitates respectfully; parody mocks. Pierre Menard in Borges's story rewrites the Quijote word for word, creating an ironic intertextual game.

mcqs.q: How do you say 'I am going to visit Spain' in Spanish?
options: Voy a visito España.
Durante always.
Voy a visitar España.
Voy visitar España.

mcqs.q: Which preposition expresses 'for' as duration (e.g., 'for two hours')?
options: Voy a visito España.
Por - 'Estudié POR dos horas'.
Durante always.
Para.

mcqs.q: How do you say 'My sister is embarrassed' in Spanish?
options: Mi hermana tiene vergüenza / está avergonzada.
Mi hermana está embarazada.
Durante always.
Mi hermana es embarazo.
